title: One-point perspective and the vanishing point
examples: How do I draw a box in perspective?
Why do railway tracks seem to meet?

steps.label: Draw the horizon
steps.note: A flat line across the page at eye level

steps.label: Mark a point
steps.note: One dot on the horizon: the vanishing point

steps.label: Draw the front
steps.note: A square facing you, like a box front

steps.label: Join to the dot
steps.note: Light lines from each corner to the point

steps.label: Close the back
steps.note: A line parallel to the front ends the box

steps.label: Rub out guides
steps.note: Erase the extra lines: a 3D box!

explain.say: Stand in the middle of a long, straight road or railway and look along it. The two sides seem to get closer and closer until they meet in one dot far away. Artists use that dot to make flat drawings look deep. Look at the board: let us draw a 3D box together.

explain.say: Why do the lines meet? Look at the board. Things far away look smaller, so the same gap between the rails looks narrower and narrower, until it shrinks to nothing on the horizon. Can you think of another place you see this?

faq.a: A vanishing point is the spot on the horizon where parallel lines going away from you seem to meet, like railway tracks or the sides of a road.
asks: Why do lines meet in perspective?
Where do I put the vanishing point?

faq.a: The horizon line is a flat line across your drawing at your eye level, where the sky seems to meet the ground or sea. Vanishing points sit on it.
asks: Where is the horizon in a drawing?
What is eye level in art?

faq.q: How do I draw a box in perspective?
faq.a: Draw a horizon line and a vanishing point. Draw a square for the front, join its corners to the point with light lines, draw the back edge parallel to the front, then erase the extra lines.
asks: How do you draw a 3D cube?

faq.a: Two-point perspective uses two vanishing points on the horizon, one on each side. It is used to draw objects seen from a corner, like a building on a street corner.
asks: When do I use two vanishing points?
How do I draw a building from the corner?

faq.a: Linear perspective was demonstrated by the Italian architect Filippo Brunelleschi in Florence around 1415 and written down by Leon Battista Alberti in 1435.

facts: Filippo Brunelleschi demonstrated linear perspective in Florence in the early 1400s.
Leon Battista Alberti described the rules of perspective in his book On Painting in 1435.

quiz.say: In one-point perspective, where is the vanishing point?

options.show: The bottom corner of the page
options.say: The bottom corner of the page

quiz.why: Vanishing points always sit on the horizon line, at eye level.

wrong.1: It goes on the horizon, wherever that line is drawn.
wrong.2: The front of the box faces you; its sides go back to the point.

quiz.say: Why do the sides of a long road seem to meet far away?
quiz.show: Road edges seem to meet because…
quiz.why: The same width looks smaller and smaller with distance, until it shrinks to a point.

wrong.1: The road keeps the same width; it only looks narrower.
wrong.2: Everyone sees this, whether tired or not.
